item.title: McDonald's brings back an iconic item from the 1980s

item.title: Hazmat team evacuates Vallejo Inn, substance tests positive as meth
item.description: An unidentified hazardous material was found at the Vallejo Inn on 444 Tennessee Street on Wednesday afternoon. After a hazmat team responded, it was later revealed that the substance tested positive for meth. The area had to be cleared while crews worked to secure the material. 5-gallon bucketThe Vallejo Fire Department said they were notified of a possible hazardous material in a five-gallon bucket at the Vallejo Inn at around 1:40 p.m. This prompted a full hazmat response, officials said. item.description: San Jose Police say they executed a raid to dismantle an illegal gambling operation this morning. item.title: Teachers, parents rally as Oakland Unified School Board weighs cuts to close $50M budget gap
item.description: Oakland parents, teachers and students packed a rally Wednesday night as the Oakland Unified School District school board considers how to close a recently revised $50 million budget shortfall for the next academic year. The district formerly projected a $100 million budget gap. item.title: Highway 101 commute hours shortened in Marin and Sonoma counties
item.description: It took only six months for driver frustration over expanded commute-hour lane restrictions on a major commuter highway, to boil over, leading to a grass-roots movement to shorten them. Many have spoken out and Caltrans took a second look to agree with them.Carpool lane hours changingSometime in late February, Caltrans will shorten and unify the HOV commute lane signs along the 52 miles of Highway 101 from Mill Valley in Marin County and Windsor in Sonoma County. item.title: Democrats, Republicans spar over ICE funding as government shutdown looms
item.description: The fallout from the White House's immigration crackdown is fueling tensions on Capitol Hill, where the possibility of another government shutdown is looming. Democrats are threatening to block a spending bill that includes billions of dollars in funding for ICE—something many Bay Area lawmakers say they just can't stomach.
